content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket. Mary Lee (E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

The notes show conflicting information:
- Notes 1-5: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write
- Note 6 (Security DB): employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read

The security note says "Security DB is the source for employment type and training." Hmm, but which is authoritative? The team memory has 6 notes. Note 6 is from Security agent, which typically has the authoritative employment type.

According to policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system. Source Code is owned by Engineer role; Analyst doesn't own it, so max = write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. With basic training, max = read.

If she is a contractor with basic security training, the max is read. Requested admin > read, so grant read.

If she is full-time, max is write, grant write.

The discrepancy matters. Which source to trust? Note 6 says Security DB is the source for employment type and training. That suggests the Security DB is authoritative. So contractor, basic training → max read → grant read.

Let me consider: notes 1-5 (HR/IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities?) all say full-time Analyst. Note 6 from Security says contractor with basic training. The Security DB is the source for employment type. So the employee is a contractor with basic training. So maximum access is read. Since requested admin > read, grant read.

I'll submit read.
